nba_directive.reason_text: This client has a 3.25% FHA rate that is almost certainly below today's market, so a straight rate-and-term refi likely doesn't pencil — the play is to make the cost of waiting concrete against their stated life goal and pin a real callback rather than letting the conversation go cold.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Lead with their specific rate and frame the FHA-to-conventional opportunity, not a rate drop
  - Their 3.25% first mortgage is a keeper — do NOT pitch a cash-out refi that would replace it
  - If they are still on FHA, surface the MIP (mortgage insurance premium) they are paying every month — ask them to pull their statement so you can calculate the exact monthly MIP cost together
  - Frame any refi conversation around eliminating MIP via a conventional refinance only if the math works net of the rate difference; coach the client to weigh monthly MIP savings against any rate increase

- Quantify the cost of waiting in real dollars tied to their stated life goal
  - Ask directly: 'What's the goal you're working toward — retirement, paying off debt, a specific purchase?' — anchor every number to that answer
  - Calculate (with the client, not for them) how many months of MIP they will pay between now and their target date if they wait
  - Example framing: 'Every month you stay on FHA, you're paying MIP you may not have to — let's figure out what that total looks like between now and [their stated goal date]'
  - If rates are a concern, introduce the break-even concept: show them how many months of MIP savings it takes to offset any rate movement

- Honor the delay but make it concrete — pin a callback, do not accept a vague 'later'
  - Acknowledge their timing: 'That makes sense — I don't want to push you before you're ready'
  - Immediately follow with: 'Can we put a 10-minute call on the calendar for [specific date 2-3 weeks out] so I can run the exact MIP savings number for you before you decide?'
  - Get a yes to a date and time — not a 'sure, reach out sometime'
  - Send a calendar invite or confirmation text the same day

- Carry the 'you can refinance again later' reframe as a pressure release
  - If they worry about locking in now: 'If rates drop further after you refi, you can refinance again — you're not married to this rate forever. But the MIP you pay while waiting is gone either way'

- Avoid these traps
  - Do NOT pitch a cash-out refi — their 3.25% rate must be protected
  - Do NOT send a generic follow-up with no new numbers
  - Do NOT accept 'waiting for rates' without running the MIP break-even math first
  - Do NOT go silent after one attempt — the pinned callback is the whole game
